runs.name: Unitil Corporation; NYSE UTL, SEC CIK 0000755001; New Hampshire public utility holding company: local distribution of electricity and natural gas to about 215,100 customers in New Hampshire, Massachusetts and Maine through Unitil Energy, Fitchburg, Northern Utilities, Bangor and Maine Natural, with the Granite State interstate gas pipeline; no rename or split seen; Aquarion Water Company of New Hampshire and Abenaki Water bought 2026-06-30 for $42.1M in cash, Aquarion Water Company of Massachusetts signed and not closed; an underwritten offering in August 2025 and an at-the-market programme
runs.box: OUT AT Q7, ON THE FLOOR
runs.entry: The v5 re-run order, unattended work-hours cycle, one dispatched analyst under the canonical brief, from scratch. The brief's departures: the repository path after the move of 2026-10-25, the lines of evidence derived by the analyst from Items 1, 1A and 7, the rivals taken from the 10-K (none named, chosen by the analyst as a CONVENTION of the run), and a line pointing to Q7, The regulated utility. Price **$55.15** (close 2026-10-23, aggregator, flagged) x **18,236,674 shares** (10-Q cover at 2026-06-30, accession 0000755001-26-000029; ATM sales after the cover date unknown, flagged) = cap **$1,005.7M**; sovereign **5.33%** (Treasury 30-year par, 2026-10-23). Read from the 10-K for 2025 (0001193125-26-042983), the 10-Q to 2026-06-30, the 2026 proxy (0001193125-26-128263) and the 8-Ks of 2025-08-18 to 2026-10-19. **Q1 IN** (five cost-of-service distribution utilities and a pipeline; allowed returns on equity 9.3% to 9.45% on about 52% equity; gas and power costs passed through; Massachusetts and New Hampshire sales decoupled). **Q2 IN** (gas the deciding part, 66.5% of five-year segment operating profit; the regulator-set return carried to Q3 as a second best by the framework's text; the castle narrowing at the margin, written down as contrary evidence: organic gas customer additions about 1,450 in 2018 to about 570 in 2025, the Massachusetts non-pipeline-alternatives burden and the GSEP cap cut from 3.0% to 2.5%, the Maine future-of-gas inquiry). **Q3 WEIGHS AGAINST, mildly** (5.4% pre-tax on added capital employed 2020 to 2025, 8.2% after tax on added equity; maintenance guess the plant depreciation provision from the stated composite rates, $61.2M a year against $146.6M of capital additions). **Q4 WEIGHS AGAINST, mildly** (ten balance sheets 2016 to 2025: net plant $883M to $1,799M, debt $416M to $926M, 60% of debt plus equity, shares 14.07M to 18.24M; goodwill small against $157M paid in 2025; no confusion; adjusted EPS featured and the EPS target set to external guidance carried to Q5). **Q5 integrity IN, ability WEIGHS FOR** (no restatement, auditor change or reserve release found; the habits read as a negative, not doubt; the general counsel appointed October 2025 an NHPUC commissioner until August 2024, recorded). **Q6 WEIGHS AGAINST** (about 60% of earnings paid out while stock is sold every year; the five-year retention test narrowly unmet on the market leg, about $0.93 per dollar retained; the 2025 offering at $46.65 inside the range and the 2026 ATM sales at $52.14 a little above its top; Part B against mildly, two pay measures reward deals and stock). **Q7 OUT on the floor**: owner cash 2021 to 2025 $50.5M a year equity-only after maintenance, -$67.0M after all spending, negative every year; the serial-acquirer CONVENTION applies ($160.4M of 2025 purchases against half of owner cash before purchases, $126.2M), so the organic pair is central, organic growth -0.33% a year from an estimate of the acquired companies' contribution (CONVENTION of the run, the filer prints no organic owner cash); growth spending $85.4M in year one, $82.9M in year ten; debt credit $27.8M a year of long-term debt against growth spending only, cap 48% the deciding part's allowed debt share (Northern Utilities and Fitchburg gas; customers standing in for rate base, CONVENTION of the run), not binding; the water companies credited at nothing and their $42.7M cost deducted; equity-only range **$24.57 to $49.60 a share** (central, a regulated utility), the best case returning about 4.8% at the price, about 3.8% all-equity; Massachusetts water beside, about -$1.53 a share more; fair price **$15.46 equity-only**, all-equity -$26.00, not positive. Q8 to Q12 not reached. Peers (the 10-K names no rival; Eversource, Chesapeake Utilities and Northwest Natural chosen as a CONVENTION of the run): average return on equity 2016 to 2025 Unitil 9.4%, Eversource 7.5%, Chesapeake Utilities 10.8%, Northwest Natural 7.9%. Facts after the stop: total debt $956.0M at 2026-06-30 against common equity $643.5M, an $86.0M term loan due 2026-10-31, $120M of notes and bonds sold since the 10-Q, covenant funded debt to capitalization not above 65%, pre-tax interest cover about 2.5 times in 2025. Framework gaps for the operator: `tools/run.py` produced nothing for the utility (it tags depreciation as UtilitiesOperatingExpenseDepreciationAndAmortization); the serial-acquirer test's basis for owner cash before purchases, and organic growth where a utility reports no organic owner cash; the utility debt credit's long-term-only rule when acquisitions and growth are funded first by term loans classed short-term; the cap's rate-base weighting the filings do not print; a deal closed after the window on the equity-only basis; Q2's regulated-return exception silent on slow, policy-made pressure on a franchise (the analyst says another analyst could defensibly have closed Q2 TOO HARD (NATURE)). Could not get: a maintenance and growth split of capital spending, organic owner cash, rate base by company, the Q3 2026 10-Q. Analyst's commits: seven pathspec commits of its own paths, one per stage, last `d6cbc82c`. Dispatcher's check: check_framework PASS; 72 ids resolve, no E-ids, no citation slip, 44 adjacent fragment pairs checked (`dispatcher_fragment_check.py`); no tracked research file over 200 KB. Contamination declared: session-start commit subjects of another company's run, a git status line naming another company's research folder, the daily digest file names, memory index lines naming no company; none used. Position note filled at the fold: not held. Armed at the equity-only fair price.
runs.narr: OUT at Q7 on the floor: five small New England gas and electric distribution utilities earning their allowed returns, but owner cash is negative after all spending every year, organic growth is about nil, and the dividend is paid while stock is sold every year; equity-only range $24.57 to $49.60 vs $55.15; fair $15.46 equity-only; no case earns the floor.
